What's the best live performance you've seen (online or in person)?

My first and only concert so far was Katy Perry in New Zealand last year. I went with my sister to it as she asked me, and I wasn't even a fan of her. I was incredibly doubtful that she would be good, as I had seen countless videos online where she sounded horrible. But she wasn't. Maybe it was a fluke, maybe it was the atmosphere making me think she was really good. But she really was. The concert as a whole was simply amazing and so fun. As someone who was only listening to metal at the time, it was hard to admit that I loved it.
Katy Perry is rad. I saw her play a venue that barely held a thousand people when she was first getting started. And I too tend towards heavier music when left to my own devices...
Despite the hate they seem to get, I must say I was impressed by Slipknot's live performances. Really nice vibe. Although now I'm saving on seeing more online so as not to spoil the actual concert :)
Saw them at Carolina Rebellion. Have to say that it is the best "festival" I've ever been too and really the only one actually... But yeah, it was amazing!

Strangely enough, Ice Cube. Came on stage exactly on time and put on a huge performance for everyone. Snoop Dogg, on the other hand, was 40 minutes late and then spent another 20 minutes trying to find girls in the crowd.

I'm not sure if you're into Korn, but on their DVD "Deuce" Ice Cube comes in to the studio to feature on their album and everybody's mind was blown at how professional he was. He's been lucky to become a movie star and a household name but he's also worked extremely hard to get where he is.

Pink Floyd, 1994. Pink Floyd in 1988 is a close second. I saw U2's PopMart, more Madonna shows than I should admit, and hundreds of other rock and blues before, during, and since, and so far nobody's even come halfway close to David Gilmour, standing full out in the rain, just murdering it atop a stage lined with a cool million watts of spinning, cascading, rotating lightbulbs.

God I'd kill to go back and do that shit again.
This. Delicate Sound of Thunder in 1988. Nothing cones close.

I live near a college town that is big on house shows (touring bands come to a house and put on a show free and open to anyone). I went to my first a few years back and it was a folky singer from kansas. He was this big burly redhead dude around 20ish who played one of those steel acoustic guitars. His voice was extremely powerful and beautiful; filled up the whole living room where he played
Leonard Nemoy with NASA and the boston pops. "Out of this world."
The Flaming Lips opening for Beck. The Flaming Lips were really the star of the show, though. Confetti, balloons, people in animal costumes everywhere. So good.

The best show I have been to was at Red Rocks in Colorado. The headliner was Beck. The opening act was, at the time unknown, The Black Keys. It was an epic performance by both and the location of course is epic as well.

I saw TheProdigy live. I don't dance... At least, I didn't until that night.

My gosh, the sheer atmosphere was immense! Those guys really know how to put on a show!

Dizzee Rascal opened, and honestly he wasn't bad.
I saw Rage Against The Machine at a festival in Ireland back in 2005 and they were thoroughly good. I also saw John Butler Trio play twice and they were flawless both times.

Sun City Girls. It was a tour after the drummer passed away I believe, they showed a little documentary and played some music. The best part was when we were walking out of the music venue and one of the singers was behind the club smoking a cigarette. Despite all of that he graciously allowed us to take a photograph and talk to him, very charming man.
I saw Rush a few years back (snakes and arrows tour) and they have aged like fine wine. unbelievable musicians.

Two best.

Red Fang on UCSD campus in one of the student hubs. I think it might have actually been called the hub. Those guys are crazy fun.

https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=WQPfQvLIseA music starts at 0:12 if you're that impatient

Next best would be the Pink Floyd cover band, Which One's Pink? Lot's of very good cover bands in LA/OC/SD

Gogol Bordello, Manu Chao and John Spencer Blues Explosion - they were all very energetic. But the most fun i've ever had at a concert was The Locos after they released their first album. After they were through with their album, they played a few covers and i think some ska-p songs but the crowd wanted more so the just repeated the setlist - it was a very fun and sweaty evening

Ok, I've got an obscure one.

Russkaja are a weird ass hybrid of Ska/Metal/Russian/Gypsy style.

They're more popular in Europe/Russia than english speaking countries I believe. An Austrian friend introduced them to me, and eventually I spotted a date they were doing in the UK at Boomtown Festival. So I managed to get a few friends together and we all went down for the whole weekend. When they came on, there must've been like 30 people watching them tops, nobody knew who they were. However about 5 songs later and the stage was practically full from people who were just passing by and realized how awesome these European Red Rockers were. There was so much love and jumping around, not to mention the songs sound fucking awesome.

Check 'em out

Kate Tempest at Best Kept Secret 2015. Never heard of her, but I decided to just give her a shot. She was absolutely amazing, the whole crowd was super into it and the atmosphere was amazing. It was like she had infinite energy.
The Grateful Dead 1984 Alpine Valley Music Theater in East Troy, WI.
Leonard Cohen (dublin gig) was the nearest a concert has ever come to being a spiritual performance for me

Rodrigo y Gabriella at the Flynn in Burlington, VT was amazing, and the only other comparable one was Reggie Watts at the same place.

The Wailers were really good in Firenze, Italy for Bob Marley's birthday in 2010 was really good, but it was more the vibe than the music.

Converge. 2010. Worcester Palladium.

It was exquisite, sweaty violence. People were diving off the stage like mad. The pit was huge. Everyone was jumping off things.

[web - flash] Renegade Racing - a stunt driving MHIMWS which keeps things interesting with fun cars and secondary goals

Like Cyclomaniacs, posted previously, Renegade Racing is a side scrolling racer in a genre which I'm referring to as My Head Is My Weak Spot, despite the fact that in Renegade Racing you don't have a head or a weak spot.

Never mind that. Renegade Racing doesn't have the scope of Cyclomaniacs 2, but it does a great job of keeping the races fast-paced and challenging, while giving a point to doing all the stunts - for later races you're really going to need the turbo from those stunts in order to get into the top positions. There are also some optional goals which reward you with unlocks and additional money and keep you from just doing same thing over and over again.
